body:
Do you still get the same error if you do it the other way around:

``` js
import {Component}, React from 'react';
```

That is not valid syntax.

Gives `Unexpected token` from Babel. ESLint throws fatal error, `Parsing error: Unexpected token`.
Correct. `import {Component}, React from 'react';` is not valid syntax and doesn't work.
Ah, sorry, not using es6 myself, so wasn't aware of that. In that case, it sounds like a bug. @eslint/eslint-team how should this be fixed?

I think the rule should check members inside of curly braces.
On ESTree, the rule should check only [ImportSpecifier](https://github.com/estree/estree/blob/master/es6.md#importspecifier)s. The `React` is a `ImportDefaultSpecifier`.

Ah, I meant about sorting inside of one import declaration.
I'm thinking sorting of declarations should keep as is.

issue.title: Fix: `sort-imports` warned between default and members (fixes #5305)
